To gain a deeper understanding of the B-physics field, particularly in search for hints of physics beyond the Standard Model, precise B^0_s meson lifetime measurements are crucial. The B^0_s lifetime is influenced by the one-loop process, which involves the rare decay of the $b$ quark into an $s$ quark and two gluons. The rate of this process is directly linked to the $B^0_s$ meson lifetime and is sensitive to new physics due to the large mass of the $b$ quark. At the LHC, the $B^0_s$ meson lifetime can be determined through various methods, including reconstructing $B^0_s \to J/\psi \phi$ and $B^0_s \to D^0 \overline{D^0}$ decplings, measuring the $B^0_s \to \psi \phi$ decay, and utilizing data from LHCb, CMS, and ATLAS experiments. The latest results from these experiments, which have been combined to produce the most accurate $B^0_s$ meson lifetime to date, will be presented in this paper.

This research examines the challenges in ensuring the convergence of a semi-discrete approximation for optimal stochastic storage and switching problems when dealing with data that is inherently irregular. To address this issue, we develop a fully discrete numerical scheme and prove the existence of solutions for the discrete problem. The main achievement is that approximating controls and state variables can be shown to converge to solutions of the original continuous problem, provided certain technical conditions are met.

Our analysis of the KASCADE-Grande data, spanning from 4 EeV to 30 EeV, reveals that the anisotropy in the directional distribution of cosmic rays exhibits a distinct asymmetry. This asymmetry is effectively modeled by a periodic dipole, with its amplitude displaying varying trends tied to the primary composition of cosmic rays at different energy levels. Specifically, the amplitude exhibits a steady decline up to 20 EeV, thereafter rising towards the 30 EeV data point, consistent with the anticipated transition zone for the dipole.

The PHENIX Collaboration at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider has conducted extensive studies in Au+Au collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 200 GeV, investigating the interplay between collisions' centrality and the average transverse momentum from p+ p to A u + A + collisions. By analyzing p T dependence of the R p T modification in p r + p p + A u + A + collisions, we observed its variation with centrality from most peripheral to most central. Notably, in peripheral collisions, the R p T modification exhibits a distinct peak at intermediate transverse momentum, whereas this peak becomes less apparent in central collisions. The observed peak in peripheral collisions aligns with expectations from the color glass condensate and gluon saturation models. The peak's shift towards lower transverse momentum in central collisions indicates an increase in medium density.

The equivalence of the theorems in noncommutative and commutative quantum mechanics is demonstrated, specifically how the noncommutative coordinates function as differential operators within a momentum space that exhibits commuting properties. Furthermore, the correspondence between noncommutative coordinate and momentum operators is established, and this is illustrated using the harmonic oscillator system. Notably, this study shows that the noncommutative oscillator's spectrum is directly related to the Hermite polynomials in a specific argument that involves the oscillator frequency, Planck's constant, and noncommutative parameters.

The algorithm in question employs a modified version of the YOLO object detection network. The evaluation of the algorithm's performance involved a comprehensive data set consisting of 1200 fields of view, each measuring 100x100 micrometers. The results showed that the object detection algorithm's precision and recall matched the human experts' annotations. The evaluation also showed that the algorithm was able to accurately detect tumor infiltrating lymphocytes within the tissue sections. This paper proposes a new algorithm, Joint WDFE and MLSE (JWMLSE), that seamlessly integrates the WDFE and MLSE (WMLE) algorithms for burst-error-prone optical communication systems. As the JLSE and JWMLE algorithms are the low-complexity versions of the WMLE, the superior performance of the WMLE can be achieved by JWMLSE, thus improving the performance of the JMLE and low-complexity WMLE. Simulations demonstrate that the JWMLSE algorithm significantly reduces the BER performance of the JMLE by 2.5 dB at a $10^{-2}$ FEC threshold, thus confirming the advantage of the JWMLSE algorithm. Moreover, the JWMLSE algorithm's performance is comparable to the low-complexity WMLSE, but the JWMLSE algorithm's performance is significantly better than the JMLE by 2.5 dB at a $10^{-2}$ FEC threshold, thus confirming the advantage of the JWMLSE algorithm. Moreover, the JWMLSE algorithm's performance is comparable to the low-complexity WMLSE, but the JWMLSE algorithm's performance is significantly better than the JMLE by 2.5 dB at a $10^{-2}$ FEC threshold, thus confirming the advantage of the JWMLSE algorithm.

The ADOpt is a innovative, filter-dilation-aware pruning algorithm that is the first of its kind to operate on graph neural networks. This paper provides key insights into the structure of finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebras, specifically expressing their left-symmetric nilpotency and solvability dimensions in terms of a basis and the structure product $\gamma$. Additionally, this research establishes a direct relationship between the nilpotency and solvability of a Zinbiel algebra $\left(V,\cdot\right)$ and its associated Lie algebra $\left([V,V],\left[x,y\right]=2\cdot x,y\right]$. Finally, several necessary conditions for a Zinbiel algebra to be nilpotent or solvable are identified.

Lattice gauge theories enable the calculation of the quark number susceptibility from first principles, which in turn allows the connection between susceptibility and particle number fluctuations in hadronic equilibrium to be utilized. This connection, however, is affected by volume effects that need to be accounted for through corrections to the volume finite data, as different methods for calculating the quark number susceptibility give varying results for the finite volume. As the quark number susceptibility ratios are less sensitive to volume effects in the deconfined phase, these volume effects are estimated based on that assumption. Furthermore, as the quark number susceptibility ratios are highly sensitive to fluctuations in the energy density, this study investigates their potential to provide insights into the properties of the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy-ion collisions, with results from the Energy Loss Fluctuations (ELn) model showing good agreement with experimental data for various collision systems and energies. This level of agreement suggests that current models for hadronization may be accurate enough to allow for the extraction of quark number symmetry from experimental data in the deconfinement phase.

We extend our previous work on computing exact correspondences for inductive modal logic formulas by considering first-order correspondences within (D)LE formulas that incorporate quantification and nesting. To achieve this, we leverage an adaptation of the ALBA algorithm, which enables the systematic computation of all potential first-order correspondences for a given (D)LE formula $\varphi$. This computation involves exploring an ALBA diagram that represents $\varphi$ and identifying its 'zombies' - the minimal correspondences from which all other correspondences are derived. The revised ALBA algorithm efficiently locates these zombies by systematically exploring the potential correspondences. To further optimize this process, we introduce a new variant of the ALBA algorithm that utilizes an enhanced ordering system, allowing it to compute the zombie correspondences using the minimal modal expansions of a reduced set of atoms, rather than the full expansions.

This paper proposes a novel approach to safe and exhaustive query answerers for database systems that incorporate incomplete information. We present a framework where the truth values of database components can be uncertain, yet queries are guaranteed to be answered in that framework without producing uncertain results. Our approach leverages four-valued logic and consistent repairs to provide a direct answer to queries, rather than aggregating possibilities through a majoritarian process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by illustrating how it can be applied to missing data scenarios in genomic studies. Furthermore, we show how our approach can be adapted to handle constraints and missing data scenarios. We also establish the computational complexity of our framework and discuss its connection to the traditional CQ-answers framework. Finally, we present an algorithm for computing all consistent repairs in a database system that operates in non-deterministic polynomial time with non-deterministic access to a non-deterministic oracle.

We introduce a novel class of linear time-varying models, specifically for data influenced by exogenous time-continuous variables, and investigate the rate of parameter convergence for this class, and demonstrate the benefits of a TV-PARX model over a TV-PAR model in terms of estimation error, as well as the ability of the time-varying model to capture complex non-linear patterns and sudden shifts in data, and provide empirical evidence using real-world interest rate data, and show that a TV-PARX model can accurately represent the data and forecast future values, and also the feasibility of using machine learning algorithms, and the effectiveness of a specific estimation method known as the EM-algorithm, and establish the strong consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator, and confirm that existing results hold under weaker assumptions, and the stability of the time-invariant data generating process, and the ability of a TV-PARX model to accurately capture and project interest rates, and the reliability of the EM-ML estimator under certain conditions.

To address the challenge of robot manipulation with object pose variations,
our research aims to minimize navigation demonstrations while still allowing
robust handling of unseen objects. We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields
(NDFs), a biologically-inspired navigation field that encodes multiple objects
implicitly as a single continuous representation. This innovation enables a
single-prompt navigation demonstration to be generalizable to any object
positioned on a predefined grid. By leveraging a contact dynamics model,
NDFs can also handle unseen objects without additional demonstration. We
validate the NDF approach through both simulated and real-world experiments,
which demonstrate the successful generalization to untrained objects and
positions through touch.

The SiD Detector, which will be a key component of SiD, the proposed final detector for the International Linear Collider if it is built as the successor to the ILC's initial final focus system, will consist of a sophisticated calorimeter system. This system will be designed to provide exceptional jet energy resolution at both low and high energy levels (up to 500 GeV). The Calorimeter system will be described in detail, along with an overview of simulation processes and the calculation of energy measurements in the SiD Calorimeter system. The energy resolution results displayed in Calorimeter system simulation and subdetector simulation show very good agreement, with the former slightly overestimated by about 5 percent. The Calorimeter system's energy resolution will be discussed in relation to the physics performance of the particle colliders, including the calculation of energy measurements of jets in various scenarios.

We have analyzed the spectra of 10 red giant stars in the globular cluster Tononzintla 2, located in the Galactic bulge. By analyzing spectroscopic data, we created a new composite spectrum for the cluster and compared it to individual member spectra to determine the abundance variations among the stars. Although previous observations of this cluster were limited to the H$\beta$ line, our results from the full optical spectrum allowed us to measure the metallicity and the spread in the abundances of several elements such as aluminum, magnesium, silicon, scandium, titanium, barium, and strontium. We found that the metallicity of the cluster is moderately high at around -0.20 and the metallicity spread is quite large at 0.15 dex. Moreover, we found that the spread in the abundances of several elements is unusually high for such a high metallicity, and the ratio of [Al/Fe] in the cluster is also exceptionally high at around 0.25, which may indicate the presence of Type II supernovae in the cluster's formation history.

Recent research in theoretical computer science has highlighted the significance of Formal Proof Archives, particularly in relation to the small-world phenomenon and the robustness of network resilience. Focusing on the arXiv and the Metamath archives, we have conducted a thorough analysis of the structure of matrices that represent the mathematical dependencies between theorems. By examining the 'in-degree' of nodes in these archives, we found distinct differences between the two: the arXiv theorem network exhibits a diverse range of in-degrees with notable hubs, whereas the Metamath network displays a more uniform in-degree distribution. This observation indicates a potential limitation in the current understanding of the self-referential nature of the Metamath archive. A key characteristic of both networks is the presence of a threshold in the in-degree node nodes, which is a defining feature of scale-free networks. Furthermore, we found the average in-degree of the arXiv network to be approximately 1.5 times greater than that of the Metamath network. This difference raises questions about the underlying causes, which may be attributed to variations in how the networks are constructed or the types of theorems they contain.

The analysis of QCD in three dimensions is extended from $SU(2)$ to $SU(N)$ using a combinatorial approach for gluonic weights at the critical fugacity point. A general formula for the critical singularity parameter z_c is derived, and its expansion in high-temperature is performed. A comparison of the low-temperature Z_2 and SU(N) critical z_c values reveals a ratio of 0.7 for the transition between SU(2) and SU(N).

We investigate the performance of the TAP free energy in relation to the convergence of the approximate message passing algorithm for a specific problem, namely $\mathbb{Z}_2$-synchronization on a complete graph. Our study reveals that the TAP free energy helps characterize the set of absorbing states for the non-convergent applications of the algorithm. Moreover, it provides insights into breaking the barrier of negative magnetization that appears with complete graph synchronization. These benefits stem from an analytical derivation of the distribution of messages in the non-convergent applications of the algorithm.

The development of advanced metasurfaces is heavily influenced by the use of tailored Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions, which serve as a key step in their design and optimization process. Recent advances in machine learning have given rise to methods that efficiently address time-consuming optimization tasks, including GSTC-based approaches. Despite these developments, the GSTCs-based methods still face challenges due to the high computational costs associated with full-wave simulations, which are essential for accurately implementing these methods. In this research, we integrate the Speedy Sheet GSTC model, which streamlines the GSTC handling, with the SRA solver to significantly reduce the computational demands of metasurface optimization. This cross-domain optimization technique leverages the speed and memory efficiency of the SRA algorithm to simultaneously refine both the speed-light model and the metasurface design, resulting in a highly efficient approach that is particularly beneficial for optimizing electrically large and complex metasurfaces.

In this article, we propose an enhanced blowing-up technique for analyzing orbits near singular points in vector fields defined on manifolds. This method will be shown to be effective in proving local orbital linearization theorems for vector fields exhibiting a non-degenerate parabolic behavior.

We've developed an ultra-fast electron-liquid correlator based on a back-propagation neural network, known as eCPNN. This tool takes as input the coordinates of electrons in a system and produces potential functions capable of accurately modeling the complex spatial relationships among electrons, even when subjected to external perturbations. The underlying architecture of eCPNN consists of multiple neural networks, each employing a set of universal approximation functions to estimate potential components. The sum of these components yields the total potential that governs the behavior of the electron system. Theoretical validation of the eCPNN model is provided through the Hyndman-Sommers theorem. Furthermore, the training of the model is accomplished efficiently and at minimal computational expense, by leveraging an optimization algorithm to adjust the parameters of the neural networks until the model's output aligns closely with the desired target data generated from full configuration interaction wave functions. The model's design allows it to be integrated seamlessly into larger variational Monte Carlo frameworks for configuration interaction expansions. The efficacy and versatility of the eCPNN model are demonstrated through successful applications to both one-dimensional and three-dimensional systems. The model exhibits remarkable accuracy, achieving mean squared errors in the range of $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-3}$ across various systems. The model's efficiency allows it to be 10 orders of magnitude faster than traditional methods for generating wave function phases while simultaneously delivering highly precise results for total energies, with errors as low as 0.001 Hartree

Recently, researchers using Sloan Digital Sky Survey data have discovered a massive structure within the Sloan Great Wall, termed the 'Giant Arc'. To determine if this formation represents an exceptionally large cluster of galaxies or an artifact in redshift space, we employed the full 3rd Quarter Sloan Digital Sky Survey catalog and constructed a synthetic arc. Although the synthetic arc appears statistically improbable given the current understanding of the cosmic matter power spectrum, it is believed that intermediate conclusions can still be drawn without access to the complete sky survey data. Analyses suggest that the observed distribution of galaxy groups is more consistent with the assumption of random spatial distribution of halos within a broad class of models that align with Sloan Digital Sky Survey constraints. Furthermore, they indicate that the existence of the 'Giant Arc' is unlikely, as it is statistically comparable to the synthetic arc models.

We investigated the impact of a photometry system's broad field of view on measuring optical depth for atmospheric aerosols. Our research indicates that an uncalibrated wide-field photometry setup can accurately determine OZT values when clear sky conditions prevail, based on the relative brightness of the moon and a reference source within the field of view. The accuracy of this method, however, is influenced by the camera's wide-angle lens which causes a variation in sensitivity across the field of view. The impact of lens distortion on the measurement of optical depth becomes more pronounced in very wide-angle systems and off-axis configurations. Nonetheless, our method can still yield reliable results for such systems by utilizing the ratio of optical depth values across the field of view and comparing it to a theoretical two-dimensional distribution. The deviation in ratio of optical depth values can be reduced to less than 0.05 for a 24-degree field of view and under clear sky conditions with an obstruction in the sky. The theoretical model we used can also be applied to analyze the shape of the atmospheric scattering of light. The research also highlights the importance of considering the relationship between the optical depth values across the field of view and the shape of the atmospheric scattering of light, as well as the effect of obstruction in the sky on the measurement of optical depth values. The research highlights the potential of using wide-field photometry to monitor the optical depth values of atmospheric aerosols in a cost-effective and operationally simple manner. Estimating object pose in complex and dynamic environments poses significant challenges. To enhance this estimation, we introduce a novel technique called projection grouping. This approach leverages the consistency of correspondence between an image and a 3D model. By identifying coherent clusters of matching points, a robust 3D-2D projection relationship is formed. Our proposed method refines the result through a compactness-based optimization process. We achieve superior performance on benchmark datasets, particularly in challenging scenarios. Furthermore, our projection grouping framework demonstrates remarkable versatility. It can be applied to various applications, including pose estimation in incomplete and occluded objects, multi-object scene estimation, and monocular object pose estimation. In these cases, our approach achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results in comparison to existing methods.

Peridynamic kernels are known to vary significantly between different materials and conditions, hindering the generalization of learning models in peridynamics. To address this issue, we propose a new mathematical framework that interprets bonds in a material as having varying 'lifespans' and derives a new kernel formulation based on these lifespans. Analysis of the asymptotic behavior of this new formulation reveals that it can accurately reproduce the discontinuities observed in strain fields, a key characteristic of cracks. Furthermore, by incorporating the peridynamic kernel into a standard machine learning framework, we aim to reduce the number of learnable parameters and enable the model to generalize to unseen materials and conditions. By constraining shareable features to the material's bond lifespan distribution, we anticipate that material-specific components can be isolated, facilitating cross-material generalization.

Building upon Graphical Lasso (GLasso), our proposed Generative Lasso (G-Lasso) extends a statistical framework for identifying sparse patterns within a complex network of relationships by incorporating hidden variables that are not directly observable. This enhancement allows G-Lasso to effectively model a precision covariance network composed of both observable and latent components, with each having distinct sparsity-inducing penalties. By formulating an efficient optimization procedure, G-Lasso achieves a balance between these two sub-networks. Notably, our analysis demonstrates that under certain conditions, estimating a graph with G-Lasso converges at a rate of $p^{-1/2}$, matching a well-established theoretical bound. This convergence rate holds true for both well-separated clusters and clusters that are closely related. Additionally, our analysis also establishes an innovative sub-linear convergence rate of $p^{-1/4}$ for the graph estimates of clusters that are closely related. To validate our findings, a series of simulations are conducted to assess the performance of G-Lasso under varying conditions, as well as to illustrate its robustness in handling both dense and sparse relationships within the graph.

To evaluate and compare various combinations of our new approach with existing methods for computing the free energy surface of the alanine dipeptide, we conducted a series of tests using different algorithms, time steps, and sampling durations. The results from these tests were presented in a structured, reproducible format that allows for easy comparison of methods based on computational cost and the quality of the outcome. The experiment described here can be readily adapted for use with other, more intricate biomolecules.

This study investigates the dynamics of binary black holes moving through a gaseous environment using a newly developed approach that takes into account the effects of binary-black-hole-gravity interactions on the surrounding matter. The method employs numerical simulations to model a pair of black holes with equal masses moving within a gaseous environment, which is also of equal mass, situated at the center of a large, spherical gas cloud. The simulation parameters include the masses of the black holes, their initial distance apart, their initial movement towards each other, the total mass of the system, the shape of the initial gravitational field, the cloud's outer boundary, and various other factors. The results of the simulation show a range of orbital behaviors, from stable circular orbits to more complex movements, as well as the development of complex structures within the gas, such as spiral arms, as well as the release of heat and the formation of temperatures within the gas. In addition, the simulation shows that in some cases, the binary system settles into a more stable orbit, while in other cases, the system becomes unstable and leads to the formation of larger clumps of gas. The research also reveals that the initial conditions of the system have a significant impact on the orbital behavior of the binary system, as well as the development of complex structures within the gas, and that the system's temperature can reach extremely high levels in some cases, leading to the formation of jets of gas that are emitted in opposite directions. This paper investigates the long-term behavior of a damped wave equation defined on a star-shaped metric graph with varying elasticity along its branches. The elasticity of the edges' slopes is set to zero at the outer endpoints of the graph, and damping is applied solely within one of the branches. The authors analyze the damping's impact on the system's exponential stability, identifying a critical threshold related to the lengths of the graph's arms. The study reveals that if a particular relationship between arm lengths is not met, exponential stability is compromised, and a quadratic time growth is observed. Conversely, if the condition is met, the system achieves exponential stability. The proof of these findings is complex and involves both straightforward and innovative arguments. A key aspect of the analysis is that it does not require a common overlap of damped region and outer Oseledec spaces, which is an unusual requirement in similar works. The authors also discuss the implications of their results and discuss potential extensions in a related section.

This research examines the characteristics of two commonly used acoustic materials, specifically Stycast 1090SI and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA). By utilizing the through transmission technique and a through-reflect-transmission method, we measured the acoustic properties of these materials with 4.0 cm and 2.0 cm thicknesses, respectively. Our findings revealed notable differences in acoustic behavior between the two materials. Moreover, our results indicated that the measured attenuation values for both materials were lower than previously reported values in the literature.

The structure of multilayer networks is typically described using projection methods. However, these methods are subject to bias due to arbitrary choices made in defining them. A better approach is to compute node centrality within each layer, taking into account the multilayer network's interconnections. Yet, existing methods fail to account for multilayer networks' unique characteristics. To address this issue, a multilayer betweenness centrality is proposed, which calculates the importance of nodes based on their presence in individual layers and their roles in other layers. This approach is further refined by adding constraints between layers to reflect the topology of multilayer networks. Computational experiments on random multilayer networks and real-world data sets demonstrate that this method successfully captures node community structures and critical nodes within each layer.

This research focuses on developing a deconvolution method to enhance the color accuracy of camera images. Traditionally, camera lenses are characterized using a metric called the point spread function (PSF), which varies across different wavelengths. To accurately represent this phenomenon, a diagonal, wavelength-dependent matrix is employed, which is supported by existing science. Thus, our proposed model extends a standard monochromatic deconvolution process to a color DeRF by incorporating a wavelength-specific deconvolution process. This is complemented by an additional process for recovering the 3D depth information from monochromatic data. The result is a single, compact deconvolution network called Depth-Accurate Deconvolution Network for Real-world Cameras (DADN-RC), which utilizes an exclusive deconvolution process to regenerate the primary RGB image from monochromatic depth data. This network is trained end-to-end to jointly optimize the camera's rendering and deconvolution processes. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our model in both image synthesis and deconvolution performance compared to baseline models.

The structure of the Dirac equation is derived within the R-Minkowski spacetime, a space that is intimately linked to de Sitter spacetime through their respective representations. By utilizing a conformal transformation, the Dirac equation is then transformed into its counterpart within the de Sitter spacetime. Furthermore, the spinor Dirac equation is also obtained within de Sitter spacetime and transformed into a form resembling the spinor Dirac equation in R-Minkowski spacetime.

We have developed the 'cdt' package, a C++ and Python implementation of causal graph modeling and learning. This package is designed to handle cyclic graphs and is comprised of two key components: the CausalNaiveBayes (CNB) algorithm for parameter and structure estimation, and the CycleMarkov (CM) algorithm for refining the model. The CNB stage produces an acyclic directed graph that serves as a starting point for the CM stage, which in turn yields a cyclic model. The 'cdt' package is freely available for download at the following URL: https://github.com/paris-tech-revues/cdt.

A type of non-contacting gas seal, the aerostatic impact seal, is widely used in high-speed rotating equipment. This study uses computational fluid dynamics to analyze the performance of an asymmetric gas supply impact seal under extreme conditions. As the seal's lips converge due to impact, the uneven gas pressure distribution causes uneven closure and uneven lubricating gas film thickness. By modifying the gas supply, the asymmetric supply can compensate for these forces, improving the seal's impact performance and preventing unbalanced wear. However, as impact speed increases, the supply cavity's pressure reduction affects the surface seal's ability to maintain separation. By adding an additional supplied channel, the channel with the larger flow rate can compensate for the closure, but this leads to an uneven film thickness that may result in uneven wear. By optimizing the supplied channels through numerical optimization, the asymmetric supply can effectively close evenly, closure angles remain below 5 degrees at high impact speeds, and the film thickness is maximized.

Using the witten boundary term method, we have calculated the charged state
spectrum of four-dimensional $R^{2}$ gravity and found that it possesses an
intriguge generalized Witten effect. This effect allows the combination of
charges $(p,q)$ to occur provided the charges satisfy the condition $pq>0$.

Mobile applications are frequently repurposed, sometimes incorporating malicious components, and often undergo minor modifications to suit new purposes or reintegrate previously removed features. These activities, though sometimes unintentional, can reintegrate previously removed vulnerabilities to the market. To tackle this recurring issue, a new security framework, OctopOS, has been developed. OctopOS enables mobile applications to be given additional features in a secure manner, allowing them to remain modular and adaptable. It allows dynamic integration of new functionality, including the restoration of features, and has been successfully implemented and showcased on the Android platform with significant performance improvements, consuming minimal extra memory and having negligible impact on runtime performance.

We've identified a novel robust online learning algorithm for stochastic episodic finite Markov decision processes with a corrupted episode, where our method achieves a specific rate of excess regret in accordance with the number of corrupted episodes, the policy support size, and the policy variance. Our approach introduces an innovative technique that incorporates gradient filtering, which our research demonstrates effectively mitigates the impact of any single corrupted episode. Notably, our study is the first to establish a fundamental lower bound showing that achieving a specific robust learning learning learning guarantee with gain correction is impossible without gain correction.

A solution to the original paradox of the mind game has been found, along with an explanation for its apparent counterintuitive nature. According to a mathematician, the solution lies in a fundamental mathematical concept that was absent in the original scenario but becomes evident when applied. The conundrum was initially presented by a British mathematician in 1990 and has been reimagined and explored in various forms ever since.

First ab initio calculations provide a comprehensive explanation for cubanite's unique characteristics, including its robust and versatile electronic structure, long-lasting mineral stability, and magnetic properties. Furthermore, the theory predicts the existence of ferromagnetic ordering within the antiferromagnetic state due to weak ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent layers. This finding is supported by recent experimental results obtained using sensitive techniques, including neutron diffraction, muon spin resonance spectroscopy, and photoemission spectroscopy.

The study proposes a method for a quantum dot and acoustic cavity system to perform reversible population oscillations between the phonon state and the ground state. Rabi oscillations are controlled through frequency adjustments of the driving laser, while sideband anomalies can be mitigated by either increasing detuning or reducing the quantum dot's coupling to the phonon. Quantum dot frequency shifts are minimized using large acoustic frequencies suitable for Rabi control, taking advantage of the phonon frequency's robustness against parameter variations. As a result, the quantum dot system achieves high coherence, making it ideal for achieving precise quantum control through Rabi operations.

A generalized Hamiltonian for the herringbone lattice is examined, allowing for onsite and bond asymmetries. By-lattice-vector blocks, the Hamiltonian's unit cell structure is simplified. Utilizing a renormalization group method, we derive effective models for various perturbations to the Hamiltonian. The methods are applied to investigate the electronic band spectrum of a NiO Ni sublattice, which contains the NiO lattice. The results for the NiO lattice's spectrum are presented and discussed.

The concept of single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) is explored, focusing on two distinct generation methods via beam splitters and parametric amplifiers. Calculations reveal that the success probabilities associated with these two methods differ, particularly in relation to the pump field's characteristics. It is found that probability of a successful outcome is lower for BSCCSs in BS scheme in comparison to PA scheme, whereas they exhibit equivalent likelihood of success when given a injected LC field. Additionally, we demonstrate that SPCCSs exhibit enhanced coherent properties as opposed to coherent states (CSs). The nonclassical nature, however, varies to some degree, depending on the method used to generate the states. The states produced by BS and PA schemes display comparable classical and quantum regions, whereas the states with LC fields exhibit the same level of nonclassicality regardless of the method used to generate them.

The provided summary translates the complex Weyl tensor coefficients' expressions from the Newman-Penrose formalism to an n-tetrad tensor component format in General Relativity. Furthermore, it represents the four Riemiemann tensor coefficients' components in the Newman-Penrose formalism using the coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the same formalism.

Researchers have long relied on approximate methods to study polymers in three-dimensional space due to the complexity of their configurations. However, a new approach has been introduced using a variational framework that represents a polymer as a sum of its constituent monomers using images generated by a graph neural network. The introduction of a loss function based on the two-body radial distribution helps train this model to predict the potential energy of interactions between polymer monomers. Our model achieves a within 5% accuracy of the traditional mean-field approximation for certain two-body probability distributions, and exhibits promising results when studying three-body correlations in a model known as the self-avoiding walk. Furthermore, this approach has been applied to study the folding behavior of proteins in two and three dimensions, showing the capability to predict the radial distribution of model proteins with accuracy.

A single ventilator can effectively breathe for multiple patients if they have shared lung compliance, as demonstrated by the equivalence $(V_{t1} + V_{t2})/2 = V_{tdesired}$, which is often achievable. However, this approach is not always possible due to the varying lung compliance of different patients. In such cases, one possible solution is to connect the ventilator to each patient through flow resistors, allowing for different tidal volumes to be delivered while still being ventilated by the same machine.

A highly lethal condition, esophageal cancer, is difficult to diagnose due to the need for time-consuming and risky image acquisition techniques. One critical step in this process is segmenting the esophagus from contrast-enhanced images, which is time-consuming and requires techniques that can handle low-quality images with poor visibility. To improve automatic segmentation, our proposed Dense Attention Unet model builds upon Dunet by incorporating three key components: global context aggregation using dense skip connections, long-term context aggregation using global attention UNet, and local context aggregation using batch normalization and bi-directional LSTM. Our method utilizes these features to enhance the context and reduce the likelihood of errors in the segmentation process. We conducted our experiments on the esophagus images from the MICCAI 2019 challenge and a patient cohort, and our results showed that our model achieved the best performance in the challenge, with a Dice score of 0.6534, and we were the only ones to successfully segment all 100 images in the test cohort.

Understanding of a reservoir's permeability structure, known as formation evaluation, is essential to optimize oil production. The conventional method involves a lengthy process of interpreting log data, which takes days to weeks. The log interpretation process is non-linear and non-convex, making it suitable for regularization with prior knowledge and the application of advanced optimization techniques. This study introduces a novel regularized model, the lm-based Inverse Model with Reduced complexity, for the formation evaluation process. A log-linear regularization model is used to ensure a smooth and monotonic production of logs, and an inverse model is designed to evaluate the formation efficiently. The algorithmic simplicity of the inverse model allows it to be trained and applied in real-time, with a response time of under 10 milliseconds. The LM-EnRML model's performance is comparable to traditional formation evaluation methods, with the added benefit of providing a smooth production curve that is easier to work with. The inverse model's ability to interpret a single well's production curve and the permeability structure of the surrounding reservoir is a significant improvement over conventional well-log interpretation. The LM-EnRML model's ability to evaluate multiple wells and the surrounding reservoir's permeability structure is a significant improvement over conventional well-log interpretation. The LM-EnRML model's ability to interpret a single well's production curve and the permeability structure of the surrounding reservoir is a significant improvement over conventional well-log interpretation.
